describes: A land recipe for any host that reports to GitHub Deployments (Vercel, Netlify, Render and others, through their GitHub apps). After a merge, wait for a successful production deployment of the merge commit, wait until the service reports that commit as the one it runs, then smoke-test it. The Lookout tab shows each stage's time and the live version against the merge.
verify: After a merge has deployed, run the deploy wait by hand from the repo root with MERGE_SHA set to the merge commit: it must print the deployment's URL and exit 0, and print nothing while the deployment builds. Point the live wait at how your service reports its commit (a /version endpoint, a header) and check it prints the commit. Then set "verified": true here, with the date and the host in "verifiedAgainst".
needs: gh authenticated (gh auth status) with read access to the repo's deployments
the host's GitHub app posting deployment statuses with an environment_url for the production environment
the service reporting the commit it runs (the live wait reads $URL/version)

steps.wait: s=$(gh api "repos/{owner}/{repo}/deployments?sha=$MERGE_SHA&environment=production&per_page=1" --jq '.[0].statuses_url // empty' 2>/dev/null) && [ -n "$s" ] && gh api "$s" --jq '[.[] | select(.state=="success")][0].environment_url // empty' 2>/dev/null
steps.note: prints nothing until a production deployment of the merge reports success; stderr is discarded so an auth error is never read as a URL
prints the merge commit once the service says it runs it; replace with however yours reports its commit
